name: Priya Menon
shortQuote: I signed my offer with Meta as a Software Engineer (E4) and you have a fair share of contribution in it.
overview: After 4 months of rigorous preparation, I finally cracked Meta E4. The process was intense but very structured. Meta focuses heavily on coding speed and system design.

timeline.description: 2 LeetCode-style problems. One medium array problem and one hard DP. Had to explain approach clearly.
Recruiter call + 1 DSA problem. Was asked about past experience and a medium-level graph problem.
Two coding problems. Trees and dynamic programming. Interviewer was friendly and gave hints when stuck.
System Design — Design Instagram Feed. Focus on scalability, CDN, database sharding.
Meta's culture-fit round. Questions around Meta's core values — move fast, be bold, be open.

tips: Practice 2–3 LeetCode problems daily, focus on arrays, trees, graphs.
System design: always start with requirements clarification.
For Jedi round, use STAR format with specific numbers and impact.
Meta values speed — practice coding under time pressure.

name: Arjun Shetty
shortQuote: Amazon's leadership principles are not just interview prep — they're actually how the company runs. Knowing them deeply was the key.
overview: Amazon's process is unique because of its heavy emphasis on Leadership Principles. Almost every round has an LP component. I spent 3 weeks just preparing LP stories.

timeline.description: Two coding questions + work simulation + work style survey. Coding was medium difficulty.
One DSA problem (linked list) + 2 LP questions. Behavioral questions were very specific.
Two coding problems — sliding window and binary search. Interviewers focus on clean code.
Design a Parking Lot system. Expected proper OOP design, class diagrams, and extensibility.
Toughest round. Heavy LP focus with one coding problem. Bar Raiser checks if you raise the bar.
Team fit discussion, career goals, and 2 LP questions. Very conversational.

tips: Prepare at least 12–15 LP stories with the STAR format.
Each story should map to multiple leadership principles.
Amazon values data-driven decisions — always quantify your impact.
For LLD, think about extensibility and SOLID principles.
The Bar Raiser is looking for someone better than the team average.

name: Sneha Iyer
shortQuote: Apple's process is the most thorough I've been through. They care deeply about product thinking alongside engineering excellence.
overview: Apple's interview is less standardized than FAANG peers. Each team has its own process. Mine involved a heavy focus on OS internals, networking, and product intuition.

timeline.description: Role overview, background discussion. Recruiter was warm and explained the team in detail.
Algorithm problem + discussion on past projects. They go deep into your resume.
Build a small app or component. Evaluated on code quality, edge cases, and documentation.
Two DSA problems — one on graphs, one on string manipulation. Whiteboard coding.
Design a distributed cache. Expected deep knowledge of consistency models.
OS concepts, memory management, concurrency. Very detailed discussion on deadlocks.
Vision alignment, why Apple, collaboration stories. Very product-focused conversation.

tips: Apple values attention to detail — quality over quantity in your take-home project.
Know your resume inside-out; they will deep-dive into every project.
Brush up on OS internals, networking, and concurrency.
Show genuine passion for Apple products — it matters.
Be prepared for whiteboard coding — practice writing clean code on paper.

name: Rahul Verma
shortQuote: Netflix's culture memo is real. They actually hire for freedom and responsibility. The interviews reflect exactly that philosophy.
overview: Netflix is different — no L1/L2 LeetCode grind. They care about how you think about large-scale systems and how you handle autonomy. The comp is top of market.

timeline.description: Detailed role and culture fit discussion. Netflix culture deck is central to the conversation.
One medium DSA problem + 30 min discussion on a past project. Focus on impact and decision-making.
Design Netflix's video streaming pipeline. Extremely detailed — CDN, encoding, adaptive bitrate, fault tolerance.
Three interviewers. Culture fitness questions — how you handle conflict, ambiguity, and feedback.

tips: Read the Netflix Culture Deck thoroughly — internalize it.
Netflix values senior engineers who can make decisions independently.
System design: go very deep on reliability, latency, and trade-offs.
Be honest about mistakes — they value radical transparency.
Comp is all-cash top-of-market — negotiate confidently.

name: Vikram Nair
shortQuote: I signed my offer with Google as a software engineer (L4) and you have a fair share of contribution in it.
overview: Google's process is long but extremely well-organized. 5 rounds in one day of on-site. They look for algorithmic thinking, not just correct solutions. Thought process matters as much as code.

timeline.description: 3 coding problems. One easy warm-up, one medium graph problem, one hard DP. Auto-graded.
One coding problem on a shared doc. Medium difficulty — binary search variant. Explain every line.
Two separate rounds, one problem each. Topics: arrays+hashing and trees+recursion. Clean code expected.
Design Google Maps routing. Focus on graph algorithms, scalability, and real-time updates.
Behavioral round centered on collaboration, handling ambiguity, and growth mindset.

tips: Google values clarity of thought — talk through your approach before coding.
Practice explaining time and space complexity for every solution.
System design: practice the full 45-min template (requirements → HLD → LLD → trade-offs).
For Googliness, prepare examples showing learning from failure.
Use Google's STAR+impact format for behavioral answers.

name: Ananya Gupta
shortQuote: Microsoft values clarity and collaboration. Writing clean code mattered more than solving the hardest problem.
overview: Microsoft interviews are structured but not overly intense. They focus on fundamentals and how you communicate your thoughts.

timeline.description: 2 coding questions — arrays and strings. Medium difficulty.
DSA problem on trees + discussion on OOP concepts.
Coding + debugging. Given a buggy code snippet to fix.
Behavioral questions about teamwork, conflict resolution, and leadership.

tips: Focus on writing clean and readable code.
Be very clear while explaining your thought process.
Prepare basic OOP concepts well.
Behavioral round focuses on teamwork and empathy.

name: Rohit Sharma
shortQuote: Uber focuses heavily on problem-solving ability and edge case handling.
overview: Uber interviews are coding-heavy but expect strong optimization and edge case coverage.

timeline.description: 2 medium-level coding questions focused on arrays and hashing.
Graph problem + discussion on optimization.
Dynamic programming problem with follow-ups.
Design a ride-matching system like Uber.
Discussion on past work and decision-making.

tips: Always discuss edge cases before coding.
Optimize brute force solutions step by step.
System design should include real-world constraints.
Practice graph and DP problems extensively.

name: Karan Mehta
shortQuote: Adobe interviews are balanced — they test both coding and core CS fundamentals.
overview: Adobe’s interview process includes coding along with strong fundamentals in OS, DBMS, and networking.

timeline.description: 2 coding questions + MCQs on OS and DBMS.
Coding problem on linked lists + OS concepts.
DSA + DBMS normalization discussion.
Behavioral + cultural fit discussion.

tips: Revise OS, DBMS, and CN thoroughly.
Practice linked list and recursion problems.
Be confident while answering theoretical questions.
Balance coding and core CS preparation.

name: Neha Kapoor
shortQuote: Flipkart interviews are very practical — they test real-world system thinking.
overview: Flipkart focuses on scalable system design and problem-solving based on real-world scenarios.

timeline.description: 2 coding questions — medium to hard.
DSA problem + follow-ups.
Low-level design — design a shopping cart system.
System design — design an e-commerce backend.
Behavioral and culture fit discussion.

tips: Focus on practical system design problems.
Prepare LLD with class diagrams.
Understand real-world scaling issues.
Practice explaining trade-offs clearly.
